Rapport

/ra-POR/ - rhymes with before · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Rapport means an easy mutual understanding between people.

By the third session the physical therapist had an easy rapport with the wary linebacker, who now saved his best jokes for her.

Worked Example

The pit crew chief and the driver debrief in a code of their own — three words, a tapped wheel, done. That rapport took two hundred laps to build, and the team measures it in seconds saved.

Rapport is a working closeness between people — mutual, earned, and specific to the pair. It is smaller than friendship and warmer than mere courtesy: two people who read each other easily and trust what they read.

How Rapport Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

chemistry

chemistry: the instant, unexplained spark between people — rapport can be built; chemistry is found

understanding

understanding: the plain word for knowing how someone works — rapport adds warmth and two-way trust

Antonyms

awkwardness

awkwardness: the fumbling distance of people who cannot read each other

stiffness

stiffness: formality that never relaxes — no give, no trust

How Strong Is It? — civility → rapport → intimacy

civility vs. rapport

civility vs. rapport: Civility is the floor — courteous, correct, and completely surface; strangers manage it in an elevator.

intimacy vs. rapport

intimacy vs. rapport: Intimacy goes further than rapport — a rapport reads a colleague's pauses; intimacy holds the private history behind them.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — rapport

Root — rapport: carried back and forth — from French rapporter, 'to bring back'

Put it together

Put it together: English borrowed rapport whole from French rapporter, 'to bring back' — Latin re- (back) + ad- (to) + portare (to carry). The buried picture is two people carrying things back and forth between them — words, signals, trust — until the path is worn smooth. The same port- root carries report, transport, and portable.

Use the root in a new word: report

Use the root in a new word: report: The correspondent files her report from wherever the story is, carrying the news back to the desk.

Word Choice

neutral / professional

Rapport is for pairs and small working relationships — teacher and class, nurse and patient, interviewer and subject — an earned, mutual ease you can watch operating. Chemistry is the instant version; camaraderie, this unit's group word, spreads the warmth across a whole crew. Rapport keeps the focus on two people reading each other well.
